company.name: Kestrel Precision Machining
company.contract: Subcontractor on an Air Force sustainment contract
environment: CNC machines on the shop floor (OT)
Part-time outsourced IT from Brightline IT

phases.name: Discovery & scoping
phases.summary: We learned how Kestrel handles CUI and drew the system boundary. The scope is the office, the file server, GCC High and the CNC network.

phases.name: Gap assessment
phases.summary: We checked all 110 controls against how Kestrel works today. The starting SPRS score was -38.

phases.name: Remediation
phases.summary: Brightline IT and Kestrel staff are fixing the gaps in order of score impact. Week 6 of about 10.

phases.name: SSP writing
phases.summary: We are writing the System Security Plan as fixes land. Some control narratives are already drafted.

phases.name: Pre-assessment review
phases.summary: We review the SSP and evidence the way a C3PAO would. We list anything an assessor might flag.

phases.name: Evidence & interview prep
phases.summary: We build the evidence binder and practice assessor interviews with your team.

phases.name: Continuous monitoring
phases.summary: After the assessment, we help Kestrel keep controls working and close any POA&M items within 180 days.

3.1.1.note: Only named employees have Microsoft 365 GCC High accounts. Shared logins were removed in August.

3.1.2.note: Roles in GCC High limit what each person can do. Engineering can see CUI drawings; sales cannot.

3.1.3.note: CUI moves only inside GCC High today. Rules for email to outside parties are still being written.

3.1.4.note: Ordering, approving and paying for CUI jobs are split between two people. Written in the access policy.

3.1.5.note: Staff get the least access needed for their job. Quarterly review is on the calendar.

3.1.6.note: IT staff use separate admin accounts. Daily work uses normal accounts.

3.1.7.note: Normal users cannot install software or change settings. Admin actions are logged.

3.1.8.note: Accounts lock after five failed sign-ins in GCC High and on the file server.

3.1.9.note: The sign-in warning banner is on laptops and the file server, but not yet on shop-floor kiosks.

3.1.10.note: Laptops lock after 10 minutes idle through Intune. Kiosks lock after 15 minutes.

3.1.11.note: Remote and VPN sessions end after 30 minutes idle.

3.1.12.note: Remote work uses the company VPN with named users and logging. Remote desktop from the internet is blocked.

3.1.13.note: The VPN encrypts all remote traffic with approved settings.

3.1.14.note: Remote users go through the VPN. Two older laptops still allow direct cloud access and are being moved.

3.1.15.note: Brightline IT staff reach admin tools only through the VPN with MFA and a ticket.

3.1.16.note: Office Wi-Fi needs approval for each device. Guest Wi-Fi is separate from the office network.

3.1.17.note: Wi-Fi uses WPA3 Enterprise with user sign-in and encryption.

3.1.18.note: Only company phones and laptops enrolled in Intune can reach CUI. Personal phones are blocked.

3.1.19.note: Company laptops and phones are encrypted with BitLocker or device encryption and checked by Intune.

3.1.20.note: Outside systems that touch CUI are listed. Only the prime contractor portal is approved.

3.1.21.note: USB drives are blocked on office PCs. CNC controllers still accept USB for loading programs.

3.1.22.note: Dana approves anything posted on the website. CUI is not allowed there.

3.2.1.note: All 38 staff finished CUI awareness training in September. Records are saved.

3.2.2.note: IT, managers and CUI handlers took role-based training. Foreman Ray Delgado took the shop-floor version.

3.2.3.note: Insider threat training is not in the course yet. Linda is adding a short module.

3.3.1.note: GCC High audit logs run for 12 months. The file server logs are sent to a log store.

3.3.2.note: Actions map to named users. Shop-floor kiosks use one shared operator login until kiosks get individual sign-ins.

3.3.3.note: Logs are kept but nobody reviews them on a schedule yet. A weekly review step is in draft.

3.3.4.note: The log store does not yet send an alert when logging stops. Brightline plans to add one.

3.3.5.note: Logs from Microsoft 365, the file server and the firewall sit in separate places. Brightline is setting up one view.

3.3.6.note: Report and search tools are not set up yet. They depend on the single log view.

3.3.7.note: All devices get time from an approved source. The shop-floor controllers are checked monthly.

3.3.8.note: Only Brightline admins can change or delete logs. Access is limited and tracked.

3.3.9.note: Log management rights are limited to two Brightline admins. The written procedure is not final.

3.4.1.note: A list of computers, servers, network gear and CNC machines is kept in the asset inventory.

3.4.2.note: Intune pushes locked-down settings to all laptops. Drift is flagged.

3.4.3.note: Changes now go through a ticket and approval by Brightline and Dana. A change log exists.

3.4.4.note: Security checks before changes are written into the change form. Used on the last four changes.

3.4.5.note: Only Brightline admins can change system settings. Changes need a ticket.

3.4.6.note: Unneeded programs and ports are turned off on laptops and the server.

3.4.7.note: Games, file sharing tools and unused services are removed or blocked.

3.4.8.note: Laptops use an approved software list. The file server and kiosks do not have allow-listing yet.

3.4.9.note: Staff cannot install software on laptops. The same rule is not yet applied to kiosks.

3.5.1.note: Each person has a unique user ID. Shared accounts on office PCs are gone.

3.5.2.note: Sign-in is checked for each user and device before access to CUI.

3.5.3.note: MFA is on for all office and remote sign-ins. Shop-floor kiosks sign in with a password only.

3.5.4.note: Sign-in uses modern methods that block replay attacks. Older sign-in methods are off.

3.5.5.note: User IDs are never reused. HR and IT follow the onboarding checklist.

3.5.6.note: Accounts unused for 90 days are disabled. The check runs monthly.

3.5.7.note: Passwords need 14 characters. Common passwords are blocked.

3.5.8.note: Users cannot reuse their last 24 passwords.

3.5.9.note: New accounts get a one-time password that must be changed at first sign-in.

3.5.10.note: Passwords are stored as protected hashes. They are never sent in clear text.

3.5.11.note: Sign-in screens hide passwords on laptops. The shop kiosk software shows characters briefly.

3.6.1.note: The Incident Response Plan is approved. It names who to call and how to handle an incident.

3.6.2.note: The plan lists DoD reporting within 72 hours. Contacts for the Air Force prime are in the plan.

3.6.3.note: No tabletop exercise has been run yet. One is booked for November.

3.7.1.note: Maintenance on CNC machines and PCs is logged. Ray's team and Brightline both follow the log.

3.7.2.note: Tools used for service are approved. Outside techs are escorted and logged.

3.7.3.note: Machines that leave for repair are not wiped first. A cleaning step is being added.

3.7.4.note: Diagnostic tools and media from vendors are not scanned before use yet.

3.7.5.note: Remote vendor support needs approval, MFA and a session log. Sessions end when the work ends.

3.7.6.note: Vendor techs are not yet checked for access. A sign-in and approval sheet is in draft.

3.8.1.note: CUI drawings are printed only in the front office. Paper is locked in a cabinet.

3.8.2.note: Only approved staff can reach CUI paper and drives. Key control is logged.

3.8.3.note: Old drives and printed CUI have no approved disposal method yet. Brightline is getting a shredding and wipe vendor.

3.8.4.note: CUI marking is in use on new drawings. Older files still lack markings.

3.8.5.note: Paper and drive logs track who has CUI media. Not yet applied to all older media.

3.8.6.note: CUI on portable drives must be encrypted. The check is manual, not yet automated.

3.8.7.note: USB storage is blocked on office PCs. Only company-issued encrypted drives are allowed.

3.8.8.note: Personal USB drives are banned in policy. Technical blocks are not on the shop floor.

3.8.9.note: Backups are encrypted and kept off site in GCC High. The server backup test is not complete.

3.9.1.note: New hires get a background check before CUI access. Records are on file.

3.9.2.note: When someone leaves, access ends the same day. Linda and Marcus use a shared exit checklist.

3.10.1.note: The building has badge locks. Only approved staff can enter the office and CUI areas.

3.10.2.note: Cameras and alarms cover doors and the server closet. Footage is kept 30 days.

3.10.3.note: Visitors sign in and wear badges. A staff member escorts them.

3.10.4.note: Badge and visitor logs are kept for one year. Logs are reviewed monthly.

3.10.5.note: Keys, badges and codes are issued and removed by Linda. Records are current.

3.10.6.note: The remote-work rules for staff who open CUI at home are in draft. Only three people do this.

3.11.1.note: Dana approved the first risk assessment in September. It covers the CUI systems and shop floor.

3.11.2.note: Brightline scans laptops and the server each month. The first full scan ran on September 12.

3.11.3.note: Scan findings are fixed within 30 days for high risks. A tracker lists open items.

3.12.1.note: Eagle Ridge assessed all 110 controls in the gap assessment. The next check is the pre-assessment review.

3.12.2.note: Open gaps are tracked in a plan of action. Dates and owners are set for each item.

3.12.3.note: Monthly status reviews with Dana are on the calendar. Control checks are logged.

3.12.4.note: The SSP draft v0.3 is in progress. About half of the control narratives are written.

3.13.1.note: The firewall guards the office edge. Rules are reviewed each quarter.

3.13.2.note: The network design is documented. Office, guest and server traffic are split by VLAN.

3.13.3.note: User and admin functions are split by role. Admin tools are not on regular PCs.

3.13.4.note: Folder access is by role. The old file server still has some open shared folders.

3.13.5.note: Public web pages and email are hosted outside the CUI network.

3.13.6.note: CNC machines still share a network with office PCs. A separate OT network with deny-by-default rules is planned.

3.13.7.note: VPN split tunneling is turned off. Remote traffic goes through company controls.

3.13.8.note: Email, files and VPN traffic are encrypted in transit. Weak protocols are turned off.

3.13.9.note: Sessions time out on firewall and Wi-Fi. Settings on the older shop switch are still being checked.

3.13.10.note: Keys for encryption are stored in GCC High and rotated each year.

3.13.11.note: GCC High and laptops use FIPS-validated encryption. The file server drive still needs a FIPS-validated mode.

3.13.12.note: Conference room cameras and microphones are not yet controlled. Policy and a physical cover are planned.

3.13.13.note: Browser rules are set on laptops. Kiosk browsers and the file server are not covered yet.

3.13.14.note: Phones use Teams in GCC High. Old desk phones are being retired.

3.13.15.note: Email, Teams and web sessions use certificates to prove who they come from.

3.13.16.note: Laptops are encrypted. The file server data drive is not encrypted at rest yet.

3.14.1.note: Windows updates install within 14 days. Brightline reports patch status monthly.

3.14.2.note: Defender runs on laptops and the server. Reports go to Brightline.

3.14.3.note: Brightline gets security alerts from Microsoft and CISA. Dana gets a monthly summary.

3.14.4.note: Antivirus rules update every day. Brightline reviews failures.

3.14.5.note: Defender scans files on a schedule and on open. Full scans run weekly.

3.14.6.note: Email filtering blocks risky messages. Firewall alerts cover inbound traffic.

3.14.7.note: Alerts flag odd sign-ins. Brightline checks them within one business day.

activity.text: Turned on MFA enforcement for two remaining admin accounts.
Reviewed Brightline's firewall rules and sent three change requests.
Finished CUI training records for the last four employees.
Mapped all 14 CNC machines and their network ports for OT planning.
Drafted SSP narratives for the Access Control family.
Set Windows update rings to patch laptops within 14 days.
Ran the first full vulnerability scan of laptops and the file server.
Held the Phase 3 kickoff and ranked fixes by score impact.
Started the visitor sign-in and badge log review.
Delivered the Gap Assessment Report. Starting SPRS score is -38.
Exported Intune and conditional access settings as evidence.
Walked the shop floor with Chris to list CUI handling points.
Signed the scope memo that defines the CUI boundary.
Kicked off the engagement with Dana and the Kestrel team.

documents.name: Gap Assessment Report
documents.summary: Results of the 110-control review, ranked by score impact. Starting SPRS score: -38.

sections.heading: What we found
sections.body: Kestrel had strong cloud basics in GCC High. The biggest gaps were on the shop floor, in audit logging and in written procedures. We rated each control met, partial or not met.

sections.heading: Biggest score risks
sections.body: The five-point gaps came first: MFA on kiosks, FIPS encryption on the file server, log correlation, media disposal and OT network separation. Fixing these moves the score the most.

sections.heading: How we ranked the work
sections.body: We sorted fixes by score points, effort and cost. Quick policy wins went first so Brightline could focus on technical changes.

documents.name: SPRS Score Worksheet
documents.summary: Running score from current control status. Today's estimate is 56, up from -38.

sections.heading: Current score
sections.body: Kestrel's estimated SPRS score is 56 out of 110. 77 controls are met and 33 are open. The score is calculated from the DoD method.

sections.heading: What moves it next
sections.body: Closing media disposal, log correlation and OT network separation adds 15 points. MFA on kiosks and FIPS mode on the file server add 6 more.

sections.heading: Score rules
sections.body: Each unmet control subtracts its weight from 110. Two controls, 3.5.3 and 3.13.11, give partial credit. You must post a final score before the assessment.

documents.name: System Security Plan (SSP)
documents.summary: The plan that describes how Kestrel meets each control. About half of the narratives are drafted.

sections.heading: System description
sections.body: Describes Kestrel's CUI boundary: Microsoft 365 GCC High, one file server and the CNC network. It lists the Air Force sustainment contract that brings CUI in.

sections.heading: Drafted so far
sections.body: Access Control, Awareness and Training, and Identification and Authentication are drafted. Chris wrote them from Marcus's exports and Linda's records.

sections.heading: Still to write
sections.body: Audit, Media Protection and System Communications wait on fixes in Phase 3. We write each narrative after the fix is in place.

documents.name: Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M)
documents.summary: Four low-risk items we plan to finish after the assessment. Each has an owner and date.

sections.heading: What can go on a POA&M
sections.body: Only one-point controls that the rules allow. Five-point controls and most others must be met before the assessment.

sections.heading: Current items
sections.body: Log management procedure (3.3.9), vendor personnel checks (3.7.6), conference room device control (3.13.12) and network session timeouts (3.13.9). Each is due within 180 days of assessment.

sections.heading: Watching the clock
sections.body: After the assessment, the 180-day clock starts. We track each item monthly with Dana.

documents.name: Access Control Policy
documents.summary: Plain-language rules for who gets access to CUI and how.

sections.heading: Who gets access
sections.body: Access to CUI is given by job need. Dana approves each request and Marcus sets it up. Linda records it.

sections.heading: Remote and mobile
sections.body: Remote work uses the company VPN and MFA. Only enrolled company devices can reach CUI.

sections.heading: Reviews
sections.body: Marcus and Linda review all accounts every quarter. Leavers lose access the same day.

documents.name: Incident Response Plan
documents.summary: Steps to follow when something goes wrong, including DoD reporting.

sections.heading: First hour
sections.body: Anyone who spots a problem calls Marcus or Dana. Marcus isolates the device and starts a ticket.

sections.heading: Reporting
sections.body: If CUI may be affected, Kestrel reports to DoD within 72 hours. The plan has the form, the contacts and who sends it.

sections.heading: Practice
sections.body: A tabletop exercise is set for November. It will test the plan with a mock phishing event.

documents.name: Evidence Index
documents.summary: A list of proof for each control: exports, logs, records and signed policies.

sections.heading: What we have
sections.body: Evidence is saved for 77 met controls. Most items are Intune and Entra exports, training records and logs.

sections.heading: What is missing
sections.body: Open controls have no final evidence yet. We collect it after each fix, with a date and the person who captured it.

documents.name: Remediation Checklist
documents.summary: Step-by-step fixes for Brightline IT and Kestrel staff, ordered by score impact.

sections.heading: This phase
sections.body: Brightline is working on log correlation, FIPS mode on the file server and kiosk MFA. Ray's team is planning the OT network.

sections.heading: Policy tasks
sections.body: Linda is writing the media disposal and CUI marking procedures. Dana approves each one before it goes live.

nextSteps.text: Pick a shredding and drive-wipe vendor for CUI media
Approve the OT network design with Ray and Brightline
Turn on FIPS mode on the file server and test file access
Set up one log view for Microsoft 365, the server and the firewall
Send the November tabletop exercise invite to managers
